@graph.name: SolarSurges NCU — Network Communication Unit
@graph.description: A Network Communication Unit (NCU) is a site-level edge gateway that aggregates row-level data from multiple Tracker Control Units and converts it for plant-level SCADA systems. The SolarSurges NCU supports Modbus RTU, Modbus TCP, IEC 60870-5-104, OPC UA, and MQTT, and provides local data buffering during SCADA outages.

additionalProperty.name: Supported protocols
additionalProperty.value: Modbus RTU / Modbus TCP / IEC 60870-5-104 / OPC UA / MQTT

mainEntity.name: What protocols does the SolarSurges NCU support?

acceptedAnswer.text: The SolarSurges NCU supports Modbus RTU and Modbus TCP for inverter and TCU integration, IEC 60870-5-104 for utility dispatch, OPC UA for industrial SCADA, and MQTT for cloud platforms. Protocol conversion is performed at the edge with sub-100 ms latency.

mainEntity.name: How many TCUs can a single SolarSurges NCU manage?

acceptedAnswer.text: A single SolarSurges NCU can aggregate up to 64 TCUs. For larger plants, multiple NCUs are deployed hierarchically and managed centrally through the SolarSurges SCADA platform.

mainEntity.name: Does the SolarSurges NCU buffer data during network outages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The SolarSurges NCU provides 72 hours of local data buffering and automatically re-syncs to the SCADA platform once connectivity is restored. This is critical for remote utility-scale plants in MENA, mountain, and offshore-grid environments.

mainEntity.name: Can the SolarSurges NCU integrate with third-party SCADA platforms?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The NCU exposes standard Modbus TCP, OPC UA, and IEC 60870-5-104 endpoints, enabling integration with third-party SCADA platforms including Siemens WinCC, Schneider Citect, GE Proficy, and open-source options like OpenMUC and OpenSCADA.
